title: openai-bridge: forward client RNG-hints and support structured-schema mapping for new Responses variants
author: Maya Chen
body: Summary: Add support in the OpenAI compatibility bridge for forwarding client-specified randomness hints and an explicit rng_seed field, and introduce structured-schema mapping to better handle the newer Responses API variants. This change ensures client requests that include 'randomness_hint' or 'rng_seed' are preserved through the bridge and honored by the serving runtime when possible, and maps new structured output descriptors from OpenAI-style Responses to Redwood's structured-output parser.
body_2: Motivation and context: The Responses family of endpoints has evolved upstream to include richer request fields (schema descriptors, function/tool-call glue metadata, and optional rng hints). Some customers expect parity between what they send to OpenAI and what we accept/forward via the compatibility layer. Previously, we dropped non-standard fields or mapped them loosely which caused reproducibility gaps and structured-output mismatches for downstream evals and tool integrations. This PR addresses three concrete gaps: 1) preserve rng-related hints so deterministic/noise-controlled workflows keep parity; 2) pass through arbitrary response.metadata keys while whitelisting known runtime fields to avoid accidental leakage; 3) add a schema_v2 mapping path for Responses variants that include typed-outputs or nested tool-call payloads.
body_3: What changed (high-level): - openai_adapter: accept and forward 'randomness_hint' and 'rng_seed' as top-level optional fields in compatibility translation. They become Decorator metadata on Redwood requests and are consumed by the runtime if the model/profile supports seeded sampling. - responses_adapter.py: new mapping table for schema_v2 -> structured-output format, including support for nested arrays and typed enums. - streaming_reassembly.ts: improved backpressure handling when structured chunks interleave tool-call frames; reduces duplicate reassembly when metadata frames are present. - runtime-proxy: small defensive checks to ensure passthrough metadata keys marked safe are preserved; unsafe keys are dropped with a logged audit event. - e2e/toolcall-echo.test.js: added new scenarios covering schema_v2, rng_seed propagation, and tool-call streaming order. - docs/openai-compat.md: document compatibility behaviour and examples for RNG hints and structured-schema mapping.
body_4: Checklist: - [x] Preserve client-sent rng_seed/randomness_hint through the bridge - [x] Map schema_v2 responses to Redwood structured format (best-effort) - [x] Add unit + integration tests for mapping and passthrough - [x] Update docs and compatibility matrix - [x] Ensure no sensitive customer headers are forwarded by default - [x] Add e2e that simulates interleaved streaming tool-call frames
body_5: Commits (summary): - 3f7a2d3: initial adapter plumbing and unit tests for rng hint passthrough - 9b1e4f0: add schema_v2 mapping logic + unit test cases for nested objects - 2c0b6aa: streaming reassembly improvements + flaky test fixes - a1dff42: docs & compatibility matrix update - 7e4b9d8: address review comments, tighten validation and add audit logging for dropped metadata keys
body_6: Files changed (high level): - services/openai_adapter/openai_adapter.go (adapter translation + metadata passthrough) - services/openai_adapter/adapter_test.go (unit tests) - integrations/responses_adapter.py (schema_v2 -> structured-output mapping) - web/streaming/streaming_reassembly.ts (reassembly/backpressure fixes) - runtime/proxy/metadata_guard.go (whitelist/deny logic and audit events) - e2e/toolcall-echo.test.js (integration scenarios) - docs/openai-compat.md (compatibility guide and examples) - sdk-tests/openai-compat-smoke.ts (smoke harness) - pkg/structured/output_parser.go (small mapping helpers)
body_8:
Review conversation (highlights): 
- Ethan Park (review): "Can we guarantee that x-rng-seed will not be used to create a stable path for cross-customer state? I want to ensure seeds are isolated to the request and never persisted in cache keys."
- Maya Chen (author): "Agree; added a note and enforced that Decorator seeds are only used at runtime invocation time and are never used as keys for persistent caches (see runtime/proxy/metadata_guard.go changes). Also added an audit event whenever a non-whitelisted metadata key is dropped so security can review."

- Priya Nair (review): "The schema_v2 mapping looks good, but I worry about silent failures when types mismatch. Can we surface a structured-parse warning to the response.metadata so callers can detect mapping problems?"
- Maya Chen: "Added an opt-in 'x-compat-warnings' metadata array on the response when best-effort mapping made lossy conversions. Tests updated to assert presence when expected."

- Luca Rossi (SRE): "Streaming reassembly change fixed the duplicate reassembly race we saw in staging, but this introduced a 1% higher P99 initially in canary. Did we identify cause?"
- Maya Chen: "The P99 blip was due to a defensive await added in a hot path; I reworked the backpressure logic to use a non-blocking drain and removed the await. Re-ran canary; P99 returned to baseline. Notes included in commit 2c0b6aa."
body_9: CI and rollout notes: - Initial CI run: lint failed (openai_adapter.go formatting + missing docstring) -> fixed in follow-up commit - Unit test suite: pass - Integration e2e: two flaky streaming tests were stabilized by the reassembly change - Canary: deployed to 'staging-region-2' with 5% traffic for 48h, observed no customer-facing errors and no incidents; small P99 blip was addressed and reverified - Rollout: merged to main and promoted to canary for dedicated clusters; feature gated by 'openai_compat_v2' flag for private installs so clusters can opt-in per-upgrade.
body_10: Security and privacy: We explicitly do NOT forward arbitrary headers; only a whitelisted set of metadata keys are preserved. The guard makes it easy to add entries after security review. Audit events are emitted when keys are dropped to allow security compliance verification. No customer secrets are stored or persisted by this change. The code path explicitly prevents using rng_seed values as cache keys or identifiers.
